paragraphs: Miami travels to Minnesota without De’Von Achane, removing a major rushing and receiving stressor from an offense trying to build on last week’s momentum. The Vikings have their own significant absence with Justin Jefferson ruled out, forcing their passing game to redistribute targets against a Dolphins defense that can now devote attention elsewhere. Brian Flores’ aggressive pressure packages remain a defining challenge for Miami, so protection, quick answers and which offense adapts more efficiently to losing its premier playmaker should drive the afternoon.

LevLine 3.0 gives the Vikings a 81.4% win probability over the Dolphins. That official probability translates to a probability-implied presentation line of Minnesota Vikings -11.5, a market line of Minnesota Vikings -10.0, and an approximate coherent score of MIN 28 – MIA 16. With both offenses missing elite playmakers, protection and replacement production become decisive, especially against a Minnesota defense built to create pressure and force hurried decisions.
